questions.title: Hello World
questions.statement: Print the exact text Hello, World! once.

examples.explain: System.out.println prints the text and a newline.

mistakes: Forgetting the semicolon
Printing with print instead of println leaves no newline
hints: Use System.out.println with the exact text.

questions.title: Name and age
questions.statement: Read a name and an age, then print Name: <name>, Age: <age>.
questions.input: A name on one line, then an integer age.
constraints: Name has no spaces in these tests.

examples.explain: Read the token and the integer, then concatenate.

mistakes: Using nextLine after nextInt without consuming the newline
hints: next() reads one token; nextInt() reads the number.

questions.title: Swap two numbers
questions.statement: Read two integers and print them swapped on one line.

examples.explain: Swap using a temporary variable, then print.

mistakes: Overwriting one value before saving the other
hints: Either use a temp variable or just print in reverse order.

questions.title: Arithmetic calculator
questions.statement: Read two integers and print their sum, difference, product and integer quotient, each on its own line.
questions.input: Two integers a and b (b not zero).
questions.output: Four lines: sum, difference, product, quotient.

examples.explain: Use +, -, *, and integer division.

mistakes: Using int multiplication that overflows
hints: Use long for the product.

questions.title: Even or odd
questions.statement: Read an integer and print Even if it is divisible by 2, otherwise Odd.

examples.explain: n % 2 == 0 means even, including negatives.

mistakes: Using n % 2 == 1 fails for negative odd numbers
hints: Compare the remainder with 0, not with 1.

questions.title: Positive, negative or zero
questions.statement: Read an integer and print Positive, Negative or Zero.

examples.explain: Check zero first, then the sign.

mistakes: Forgetting the zero case
hints: Three branches; zero is neither positive nor negative.

questions.title: Largest of three
questions.statement: Read three integers and print the largest one.

examples.explain: Compare pairwise or use Math.max.

mistakes: Initialising the maximum to 0 breaks all-negative input
hints: Math.max nests cleanly.

questions.title: Leap year
questions.statement: Read a year and print Leap or Not leap using the Gregorian rule.

examples.explain: Divisible by 4, and not by 100 unless also by 400.

mistakes: Only checking divisibility by 4 turns 1900 into a leap year
hints: Combine the 4/100/400 conditions with && and ||.

questions.title: Simple calculator
questions.statement: Read a, an operator (+ - * /), and b. Print the result. For division by zero print cannot divide by zero.
questions.output: The result, or the error line.

examples.explain: Switch on the operator character.

mistakes: Dividing before checking zero
Forgetting charAt(0) to read the operator
hints: Read the operator as a String token, then charAt(0).

questions.title: Multiplication table
questions.statement: Read n and print its table from 1 to 5 in the form n x i = product.

examples.explain: Loop i from 1 to 5 and print each line.

mistakes: Printing the product without parentheses can concatenate instead of multiplying
hints: Parenthesise n * i inside the concatenation.

questions.title: Factorial
questions.statement: Read n and print n! using a loop.

examples.explain: Accumulate 1 * 2 * ... * n; 0! is 1.

mistakes: Using int overflows after 12!
hints: Start from 1 and use long.

questions.title: Fibonacci series
questions.statement: Read n and print the first n Fibonacci numbers separated by spaces, starting 0 1.

examples.explain: Each term is the sum of the previous two.

mistakes: Printing n+1 terms
Using int for large Fibonacci values
hints: Keep two variables and append to a StringBuilder.

questions.title: Prime number
questions.statement: Read n and print Prime if it is prime, otherwise Not prime.

examples.explain: Test divisors up to sqrt(n); 0 and 1 are not prime.

mistakes: Treating 1 as prime
Looping to n instead of sqrt(n)
hints: Reject n < 2 first.

questions.title: Palindrome number
questions.statement: Read n and print Palindrome if it reads the same reversed, otherwise Not palindrome.

examples.explain: Reverse the digits and compare with the original.

mistakes: Comparing after n has been reduced to 0
hints: Save the original value before reversing.

questions.title: Reverse a number
questions.statement: Read n and print its digits reversed. Leading zeros disappear (1200 becomes 21).

examples.explain: reversed = reversed * 10 + last digit.

mistakes: Trying to keep leading zeros in an int
hints: 0 prints 0 with this loop.

questions.title: Sum of digits
questions.statement: Read a non-negative integer and print the sum of its digits.

examples.explain: Peel digits with % 10 and / 10.

mistakes: Forgetting that 0 needs no loop and sums to 0
hints: The loop body runs zero times for 0, which is correct.

questions.title: Armstrong number
questions.statement: Read n and print Armstrong if it equals the sum of its digits each raised to the number of digits, otherwise Not Armstrong.
mistakes: Using a fixed power of 3 instead of the digit count
hints: Count digits first; 0 is a one-digit Armstrong number.

questions.title: Perfect number
questions.statement: Read n and print Perfect if it equals the sum of its proper divisors, otherwise Not perfect.

examples.explain: Proper divisors 1, 2, 3 sum to 6.

mistakes: Counting n itself as a proper divisor
hints: For n = 1 the proper-divisor sum is 0, so it is not perfect.

questions.title: GCD
questions.statement: Read two positive integers and print their greatest common divisor.

examples.explain: Euclid: gcd(a,b) = gcd(b, a % b).

mistakes: Using subtraction only, which is slow
hints: Loop while b is not zero.

questions.title: LCM
questions.statement: Read two positive integers and print their least common multiple.

examples.explain: lcm = a / gcd * b.

mistakes: Multiplying before dividing, which can overflow
hints: Divide by gcd first: a / gcd * b.

questions.title: Star triangle
questions.statement: Read n and print a left-aligned triangle of stars with n rows.
questions.output: n lines; row r has r stars.

examples.explain: Row r prints r stars.

mistakes: Printing a newline inside the inner loop
hints: Build each row, print it once.

questions.title: Number pattern
questions.statement: Read n and print rows 1 to n; row r contains the numbers 1 to r separated by spaces.

examples.explain: Inner loop runs from 1 to r.

mistakes: Leaving a trailing space that changes the expected output
hints: Append the space before every number except the first.

questions.title: Vowel or consonant
questions.statement: Read one character and print Vowel, Consonant or Not a letter. Treat a, e, i, o, u in either case as vowels.
constraints: Input is a single character token.

examples.explain: Lowercase the character before checking.

mistakes: Forgetting uppercase vowels
hints: Character.toLowerCase handles case.

questions.title: Reverse a string
questions.statement: Read one line and print it reversed.

examples.explain: Reverse with StringBuilder.

mistakes: Building the reverse with += inside a loop
hints: StringBuilder.reverse is the direct tool.

questions.title: Vowel counter
questions.statement: Read one line and print how many vowels it contains, in either case.

examples.explain: Count a, e, i, o, u ignoring case.

mistakes: Counting only lowercase input
hints: Lowercase the line once, then check one string of vowels.

questions.title: Word count
questions.statement: Read one line and print the number of words (split on whitespace).
constraints: Words are separated by one or more spaces.

examples.explain: Trim and split on whitespace.

mistakes: Splitting on a single space leaves empty words
hints: Trim first and handle the empty line.

questions.title: String palindrome
questions.statement: Read one word and print Palindrome if it reads the same backwards ignoring case, otherwise Not palindrome.

examples.explain: Compare lowercased text with its reverse.

mistakes: Using == to compare the reversed text
hints: equalsIgnoreCase handles the case rule.

questions.title: Array sum
questions.statement: Read n, then n integers, and print their sum.

examples.explain: Accumulate every value.

mistakes: Using int for a sum that can overflow
hints: You do not need to store the array to sum it.

questions.title: Array maximum
questions.statement: Read n, then n integers, and print the largest value.

examples.explain: Start at the first value, not 0.

mistakes: Initialising max to 0 breaks all-negative input
hints: Read the first value into max before the loop.

questions.title: Linear search
questions.statement: Read n, then n integers, then a key. Print the first index where the key appears, or -1 if it is absent.
questions.input: n, n integers, then the key.

examples.explain: Scan from index 0 and stop at the first match.

mistakes: Continuing after the first match changes which index is printed
hints: Break on the first match.

questions.title: Binary search
questions.statement: Read a sorted array and a key. Print the key's index, or -1.
questions.input: n, n sorted integers, then the key.

examples.explain: Halve the range until the key or an empty range is found.

mistakes: Using <= mid instead of mid +/- 1, causing an infinite loop
hints: Compare the middle element and discard half.

questions.title: Bubble sort
questions.statement: Read n integers and print them sorted ascending using bubble sort.

examples.explain: Repeatedly swap adjacent out-of-order pairs.

mistakes: Looping j to n-1 instead of n-1-i, reading past the sorted tail
hints: After pass i, the last i elements are sorted.

questions.title: Selection sort
questions.statement: Read n integers and print them sorted ascending using selection sort.

examples.explain: Find the minimum of the unsorted suffix and swap it into place.

mistakes: Swapping inside the inner loop instead of after finding the minimum
hints: Track the index of the minimum, swap once per outer iteration.

questions.title: Insertion sort
questions.statement: Read n integers and print them sorted ascending using insertion sort.

examples.explain: Grow a sorted prefix by inserting each new value into place.

mistakes: Losing the key value while shifting
hints: Save a[i] before shifting larger values right.

questions.title: Remove duplicates
questions.statement: Read n integers and print the distinct values in first-seen order.

examples.explain: A LinkedHashSet keeps first-seen order and removes duplicates.

mistakes: Using a HashSet, which loses the first-seen order
hints: LinkedHashSet preserves insertion order.

questions.title: Second largest element
questions.statement: Print the second largest distinct value, or -1 if it does not exist.

examples.explain: Ignore values equal to the largest when updating the second.

mistakes: Updating second with a value equal to max
hints: Only update second when v is strictly below max.

questions.title: Rotate array right
questions.statement: Rotate the array right by k positions and print the result.
questions.input: n and k, then n integers.
questions.output: The rotated array separated by spaces.

examples.explain: Reduce k modulo n, then split at n-k.

mistakes: Not reducing k modulo n, causing an index out of range
hints: The new first element is at index n-k after reducing k.

questions.title: Merge two sorted arrays
questions.statement: Read two sorted arrays and print their merged sorted values.
questions.input: n m, then n integers, then m integers.

examples.explain: Walk both arrays with two pointers.

mistakes: Appending a trailing space that fails exact comparison
hints: Compare the two heads and append the smaller.

questions.title: Find the missing number
questions.statement: The numbers 1..n appear once except one missing value. Print the missing value.

examples.explain: Expected sum minus actual sum.

mistakes: Computing n*(n+1) in int and overflowing
hints: Use long for the expected sum.

questions.title: Find the duplicate number
questions.statement: Read n integers where exactly one value repeats. Print the repeated value.

examples.explain: A Set rejects the value it has already seen.

mistakes: Printing the first repeated position instead of the value
hints: add() returns false when the value is already present.

questions.title: Frequency of elements
questions.statement: Read n integers and print each distinct value and its count as value=count, sorted by value.

examples.explain: TreeMap keeps values sorted; merge counts them.

mistakes: Using HashMap and assuming the output order is stable
hints: TreeMap sorts keys for deterministic output.

questions.title: Two Sum
questions.statement: Find two numbers that add up to the target. Print their indices (i j with i < j), or -1.

examples.explain: Store seen values and look for target - current.

mistakes: Returning the same index twice when target is double the value
hints: Check for the complement before storing the current value.

questions.title: Anagram checker
questions.statement: Read two words and print Anagram if they contain the same letters with the same counts, else Not anagram.

examples.explain: Sort both words or compare 26 counts.

mistakes: Comparing arrays with == instead of Arrays.equals
hints: Sorting both makes equality a simple comparison.

questions.title: Character frequency
questions.statement: Read a word and print each character with its count as char=count, sorted alphabetically.

examples.explain: Use a 26-slot count array.

mistakes: Printing zero-count letters
hints: Only print slots with a positive count.

questions.title: First non-repeating character
questions.statement: Print the first character that appears exactly once, or none.

examples.explain: Count first, then scan in order for count 1.

mistakes: Using HashMap and losing the original character order
hints: LinkedHashMap preserves first-seen order.

questions.title: Reverse the words
questions.statement: Read a sentence and print its words in reverse order, separated by single spaces.

examples.explain: Split, then walk the array backwards.

mistakes: Keeping the original multiple spaces
hints: Trim and split on \\s+ first.

questions.title: Longest word
questions.statement: Print the longest word in a sentence; on a tie print the first one.

examples.explain: Compare lengths, keep the first on a tie.

mistakes: Using >= so the last tied word wins
hints: Strictly greater keeps the first on a tie.

questions.title: Matrix addition
questions.statement: Read two r×c matrices and print their element-wise sum.
questions.input: r c, then r*c integers for A, then r*c for B.
questions.output: r lines of c space-separated values.

examples.explain: Add matching positions.

mistakes: Printing a trailing space
hints: Read B in the same loop that prints the sum.

questions.title: Matrix multiplication
questions.statement: Read two n×n matrices and print their product.
questions.input: n, then n*n integers for A, then n*n for B.
questions.output: n lines of n space-separated values.

examples.explain: C[i][j] = sum of A[i][k] * B[k][j].

mistakes: Swapping the row/column indices in the inner sum
hints: Fix the output cell, then loop k over the shared dimension.

questions.title: Matrix transpose
questions.statement: Read an r×c matrix and print its transpose (c rows, r columns).

examples.explain: transpose[j][i] = matrix[i][j].

mistakes: Iterating rows in the outer loop, which prints the original
hints: The outer loop must walk columns.

questions.title: Diagonal sum
questions.statement: Read an n×n matrix and print the sum of its main diagonal.

examples.explain: m[i][i] for every row is the main diagonal.

mistakes: Summing the anti-diagonal as well
hints: Compare the row and column index.

questions.title: Factorial with recursion
questions.statement: Read n and print n! using a recursive method.

examples.explain: factorial(n) = n * factorial(n-1), with 0! = 1.

mistakes: Missing the base case, causing a StackOverflowError
hints: 0! and 1! are both 1.

questions.title: Recursive Fibonacci
questions.statement: Print the n-th Fibonacci number (0-based: F0=0, F1=1) using recursion.

examples.explain: fib(n) = fib(n-1) + fib(n-2).

mistakes: Returning 1 for n=0
hints: Two base cases: 0 and 1.

questions.title: Binary to decimal
questions.statement: Read a binary string and print its decimal value.

examples.explain: Result = result*2 + digit for every bit.

mistakes: Using Integer.parseInt(bits, 2) on a long input and overflowing
hints: Horner's method: shift left and add the bit.

questions.title: Decimal to binary
questions.statement: Read a non-negative integer and print its binary representation without using built-in conversion helpers.
questions.output: Binary digits with no leading zeros (0 for zero).

examples.explain: Repeatedly take n%2 and prepend it while n shrinks.

mistakes: Forgetting the special case for 0, which prints an empty string
hints: Reverse the collected remainders at the end.

questions.title: Stack implementation
questions.statement: Implement a stack supporting push, pop, peek and size. Read commands until end and print the result of pop, peek and size.
questions.input: Commands: push X, pop, peek, size, end.
questions.output: One line per command that returns a value.
constraints: Only valid commands; never pop or peek an empty stack.

examples.input:
push 5
push 3
pop
peek
size
end
examples.explain: pop removes and prints 3, peek shows 5, size is 1.

tests.name: mixed commands
tests.input:
push 5
push 3
pop
peek
size
end

mistakes: Using Stack (legacy, synchronized) instead of ArrayDeque
hints: ArrayDeque push/pop act on the head.

questions.title: Queue implementation
questions.statement: Implement a queue with enqueue, dequeue, peek and size. Print values for dequeue, peek and size.
questions.input: Commands: enqueue X, dequeue, peek, size, end.
constraints: Never dequeue or peek an empty queue.

examples.input:
enqueue 4
enqueue 9
dequeue
peek
size
end
examples.explain: FIFO: dequeue removes 4, 9 is still at the front.

tests.name: mixed commands
tests.input:
enqueue 4
enqueue 9
dequeue
peek
size
end

tests.name: empty then two
tests.input:
enqueue 1
enqueue 2
size
dequeue
dequeue
end

mistakes: Using push/pop on a queue, which makes it a stack
hints: addLast/removeFirst gives FIFO order.

questions.title: Balanced parentheses
questions.statement: Check whether (), [] and {} are correctly balanced.

examples.explain: Every closing bracket must match the top of the stack.

mistakes: Forgetting to check that the stack is empty at the end
hints: Push openers; on a closer, compare with the popped top.

questions.title: Linked list implementation
questions.statement: Build a singly linked list from n values and print them in order.

examples.explain: Append each value to the tail, then traverse from the head.

mistakes: Losing the head while traversing, so the list cannot be printed again
hints: Keep a separate tail reference for O(1) appends.

questions.title: Remove linked list duplicates
questions.statement: Remove duplicate values from a linked list, keeping the first occurrence, and print the result.
questions.output: The cleaned list separated by spaces.

examples.explain: A set tracks seen values while walking the list.

mistakes: Removing the head node without updating the head reference
hints: Filter while building instead of unlinking nodes.

questions.title: Middle of a linked list
questions.statement: Print the middle node's value (the second middle for an even count) using slow/fast pointers.

examples.explain: Fast moves two steps while slow moves one.

mistakes: Advancing slow twice, which lands past the middle
hints: Check fast != null && fast.next != null.

questions.title: Detect a cycle in a linked list
questions.statement: Read n values, then k. If k >= 0, link the tail to the node at index k (0-based); otherwise leave the list acyclic. Print Cycle or No cycle.
questions.input: n and k, then n integers.

examples.explain: Floyd's algorithm: fast meets slow only inside a cycle.

mistakes: Comparing values instead of node references
hints: Compare references with ==, not values.

questions.title: Word frequency with a HashMap
questions.statement: Count how often each word appears and print word=count sorted alphabetically.

examples.explain: HashMap counts, TreeMap sorts for output.

mistakes: Using == to compare words instead of equals
hints: TreeMap sorts the keys for a stable report.

questions.title: Sort objects with a Comparator
questions.statement: Read students as name and score, then print them sorted by score descending, ties by name ascending.
questions.input: n, then n lines of "name score".

examples.explain: Comparator.comparingInt(...).reversed().thenComparing(...).

mistakes: Using subtraction in a comparator, which can overflow
hints: comparingInt avoids overflow; reversed() flips the order.

questions.title: Student management system
questions.statement: Store students with id, name and marks. Print the average marks (2 decimals) and the topper's name.
questions.input: n, then n lines of "id name marks".

examples.explain: A Student class holds the data; a loop aggregates it.

mistakes: Integer division truncating the average
hints: Cast to double before dividing and format with %.2f.

questions.title: Bank account class
questions.statement: Model a bank account with deposit and withdraw. Apply the given operations and print the final balance with 2 decimals.
questions.input: Starting balance, op count, then ops "deposit X" or "withdraw X".

examples.explain: Encapsulated state only changes through methods that validate.

mistakes: Making balance public so invalid withdrawals bypass validation
hints: Validate inside withdraw, not at the call site.

questions.title: Employee inheritance
questions.statement: Employees are dev or manager; managers earn a 20% bonus. Print the total salary with 2 decimals.
questions.input: n, then n lines of "type base".

examples.explain: Polymorphic salary() gives each subclass its own rule.

mistakes: Not marking salary() as overridable or forgetting @Override
hints: Call through the Employee reference to get polymorphism.

questions.title: Custom exception
questions.statement: Validate an age. Ages below 0 throw InvalidAgeException with the age as the message; print the exception message, else "Valid age: X".
questions.output: The exception message or the valid-age line.

examples.explain: A checked custom exception carries a descriptive message.

mistakes: Catching Exception and swallowing the message
hints: Throw in a helper, catch in main where you can report it.

questions.title: File word counter
questions.statement: Write the given sentence to a temporary file, read it back and print the number of words.

examples.explain: Files.writeString then split on whitespace.

mistakes: Forgetting to close or delete the temporary file
hints: Files.readString keeps it short; delete in the same method.

questions.title: Generic min and max
questions.statement: Read n integers and print the minimum and maximum using one generic method bounded by Comparable.

examples.explain: <T extends Comparable<T>> lets one method serve any ordered type.

mistakes: Using < on T, which does not compile for a generic type
hints: compareTo returns a negative, zero or positive int.

questions.title: LRU cache
questions.statement: Implement an LRU cache with the given capacity. Read put/get commands until end and print every get result (-1 on a miss).
questions.input: capacity, then put k v / get k commands, then end.

examples.input:
2
put 1 1
put 2 2
get 1
put 3 3
get 2
get 3
end
examples.explain: LinkedHashMap with accessOrder evicts the least recently used entry.

tests.name: evicts lru
tests.input:
2
put 1 1
put 2 2
get 1
put 3 3
get 2
get 3
end

mistakes: Using a plain HashMap, which never evicts
hints: accessOrder=true refreshes recency on get.

questions.title: Custom dynamic array
questions.statement: Implement an int list that grows its backing array. Add n values, then print the size and all values.
questions.output: Size, then the values separated by spaces.

examples.explain: Internally int[] doubles when full.

mistakes: Forgetting to copy old elements when growing
hints: Arrays.copyOf keeps the old values.

questions.title: Producer-consumer with threads
questions.statement: Start one producer that puts 1..n into a BlockingQueue and one consumer that sums them. Print the sum.

examples.explain: put() blocks when full, take() blocks when empty.

mistakes: Reading a shared variable without synchronization or a queue
hints: Use a sentinel value to tell the consumer to stop.

questions.title: ExecutorService task submission
questions.statement: Read n numbers, square each on a thread pool, and print the sum.

examples.explain: invokeAll returns futures in submission order.

questions.time: O(n) wall clock with parallel workers
mistakes: Never calling shutdown(), so the JVM keeps running
hints: invokeAll blocks until every task finishes.

questions.title: CompletableFuture chain
questions.statement: Read a number and print the result of doubling it and adding 1, computed through an asynchronous chain.

examples.explain: supplyAsync then thenApply builds a pipeline; join waits.

mistakes: Calling get() without handling checked exceptions in a lambda
hints: join() throws no checked exceptions.

questions.title: Custom annotation with reflection
questions.statement: Define an @Info annotation with an author value, annotate Main, and read the value at runtime.
constraints: Annotation must be retained at runtime.

examples.explain: getAnnotation reads a RUNTIME annotation.

mistakes: Forgetting @Retention(RUNTIME), so getAnnotation returns null
hints: A missing retention policy means CLASS, not RUNTIME.

questions.title: Parse a CSV file
questions.statement: Read n lines of name,marks from a CSV. Print how many students passed (marks >= 60) and the average marks with 2 decimals.

examples.explain: split(",") gives the fields; parse the second one.

mistakes: Calling next() after nextInt() and misreading the first row
hints: Use nextLine consistently for the CSV rows.

questions.title: Parse a flat JSON object
questions.statement: Parse a flat object like {"a":1,"b":2} without a library and print its keys and values as key=value sorted by key.
questions.input: One flat JSON object with integer values.
constraints: Keys are simple words; values are integers.

examples.explain: Strip the braces, split on commas, then on the colon.

mistakes: Splitting on "," without handling the outer braces first
hints: substring between { and } simplifies the split.

questions.title: Generic repository
questions.statement: Implement a Repository<T> that stores items. Add n strings and print them joined by comma-space.

examples.explain: A generic class stores any element type without casts.

mistakes: Returning the internal list directly, letting callers mutate it
hints: unmodifiableList keeps ownership inside the repository.

questions.title: Immutable value class
questions.statement: Write an immutable Money class (final fields, no setters) with an add method that returns a new instance. Print the sum of two amounts.

examples.explain: add returns a new Money instead of mutating this.

mistakes: Adding a setter, which breaks immutability
hints: All fields final and every operation returns a new object.

questions.title: Thread-safe singleton
questions.statement: Implement a singleton counter and increment it from several threads. Each increment adds 1; print the final count.

examples.explain: A single instance with an AtomicInteger is safe under concurrency.

mistakes: Using a plain int field, so increments are lost
hints: An enum singleton is initialized safely by the JVM.

questions.title: Factory pattern
questions.statement: Use a shape factory: circle takes a radius, square a side. Print the area with 2 decimals.

examples.explain: The factory hides which class is constructed.

mistakes: Constructing subclasses at the call site, which defeats the factory
hints: A switch expression keeps the factory compact.

questions.title: Observer pattern
questions.statement: Register two observers on a subject, publish one value, and let each observer print its name and the value.

examples.explain: The subject loops over registered observers.

mistakes: Notifying from a for-each while observers unregister, causing a ConcurrentModificationException
hints: A functional interface lets lambdas be observers.

questions.title: Builder pattern
questions.statement: Build a pizza with a size and any number of toppings, then print "SIZE pizza with t1, t2".
questions.input: Size, topping count, then that many toppings.

examples.explain: The builder collects parts and finishes in build().

mistakes: Returning void from topping(), which breaks chaining
hints: Return this so calls can chain.

questions.title: Strategy pattern
questions.statement: Choose a sorting strategy by name (bubble or insertion), sort n integers, and print them.
questions.input: Strategy name, n, then n integers.

examples.explain: The algorithm is an object selected at runtime.

mistakes: Using if/else everywhere instead of a strategy object
hints: Method references fit a functional interface.

questions.title: Token bucket rate limiter
questions.statement: A bucket holds `capacity` tokens and refills `refill` tokens per second, capped at capacity. Each request costs one token. For n requests at ascending timestamps, print Allowed or Denied.
questions.input: capacity refill n, then n timestamps.

examples.explain: Two tokens at t=0 allow two requests; one refills at t=1.

mistakes: Refilling before checking the elapsed time, granting free tokens
hints: Track the last timestamp; add elapsed * refill, capped.

questions.title: Thread-safe counter
questions.statement: Start the given number of threads, each incrementing a shared counter the given number of times, then print the total.

examples.explain: AtomicInteger avoids lost updates without a lock.

mistakes: Using counter++ on a shared int, which races
hints: incrementAndGet is a single atomic operation.

questions.title: Parallel stream aggregation
questions.statement: Read n integers and print the sum of the squares of the even numbers, computed with a parallel stream.

examples.explain: 2^2 + 4^2 = 20; the pipeline is stateless and safe to split.

mistakes: Mutating a shared list inside a parallel stream
hints: Sum is a reduction, so order does not matter.

questions.title: Stream grouping report
questions.statement: Read n lines of department and salary and print total salary per department as dept=total, sorted by department.

examples.explain: groupingBy with summingLong aggregates the salaries.

mistakes: Forgetting the map supplier and getting unordered output
hints: TreeMap::new sorts the department keys.

questions.title: Reduce for a product
questions.statement: Read n integers and print their product using reduce.

examples.explain: reduce(1, (a, b) -> a * b).

mistakes: Using reduce without an identity on an empty stream
hints: Pass 1L as the identity.

questions.title: Multiple comparators
questions.statement: Sort students by score descending, then age ascending, then name ascending, and print only the names.
questions.input: n, then n lines "name age score".

examples.explain: Chained comparators break ties in order.

mistakes: Calling reversed() at the end, which reverses every tiebreak too
hints: Reverse only the score comparator before chaining.

questions.title: Coin change (minimum coins)
questions.statement: Given coin denominations and an amount, print the minimum number of coins, or -1 if it is impossible.

examples.explain: dp[a] = min(dp[a - coin] + 1) over all coins.

mistakes: Adding 1 to Integer.MAX_VALUE, which overflows negative
hints: Skip unreachable states instead of adding to MAX_VALUE.

questions.title: BFS shortest path
questions.statement: Read an unweighted undirected graph and print the shortest distance from start to end, or -1.
questions.input: n m, then m edges "u v", then start end.

examples.explain: BFS visits nodes in order of distance.

mistakes: Using DFS, which does not guarantee the shortest path
hints: Mark nodes when you enqueue them, not when you dequeue.

questions.title: Connected components with DFS
questions.statement: Count the connected components of an undirected graph.
questions.input: n m, then m edges "u v".

examples.explain: Each DFS from an unvisited node covers one component.

mistakes: Marking visited after popping, which can push a node twice
hints: Mark on push to avoid duplicate work.

questions.title: Trie word lookup
questions.statement: Insert n words into a trie, then answer q exact-word queries with YES or NO.
questions.input: n, n words, q, then q queries.

examples.explain: A trie stores shared prefixes once; mark word ends.

mistakes: Returning true for a prefix that was never inserted as a word
hints: Check the word flag after consuming every character.

questions.title: Top K frequent values
questions.statement: Print the k most frequent values; break ties by the smaller value first.
questions.output: The k values separated by spaces.

examples.explain: Sort by count descending, then value ascending.

mistakes: Subtracting counts in the comparator, which can overflow
hints: Integer.compare keeps the comparator safe.

questions.title: Sliding window maximum
questions.statement: For every window of size k, print the maximum.

examples.explain: A decreasing deque keeps candidate indices.

mistakes: Removing from the wrong end, which loses the current maximum
hints: Store indices so you can expire the window's left edge.

questions.title: Merge intervals
questions.statement: Merge overlapping intervals and print them sorted by start.
questions.output: Merged intervals, one per line as "start end".

examples.explain: Sort by start; extend the last interval when it overlaps.

mistakes: Merging only when starts are equal instead of when they overlap
hints: Overlap means the next start <= current end.

questions.title: N-Queens count
questions.statement: Count the distinct solutions to the n-queens problem.

examples.explain: Place one queen per row and reject attacked columns and diagonals.

mistakes: Using one diagonal array for both directions
hints: Columns, row-col and row+col are the three attack sets.

questions.title: Mini inventory system
questions.statement: Track inventory with add/remove commands; list prints items with positive quantity as name=qty sorted by name.
questions.input: add name qty / remove name qty / list, then end.
questions.output: One line per item on list.

examples.input:
add pen 5
add book 2
remove pen 2
list
end
examples.explain: A TreeMap keeps names sorted and merges updates.

tests.name: add and remove
tests.input:
add pen 5
add book 2
remove pen 2
list
end

tests.name: remove to zero
tests.input:
add pen 1
remove pen 1
list
end

mistakes: Allowing negative stock when removing more than available
hints: Clamp or validate after merge.
